Listen to this article Share The Governing Council of the University of Jos (UNIJOS) has appointed Patricia Mamko Lar, a professor as the institution’s 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the university’s establishment. Lar succeeds Tanko Ishaya, also a professor whose tenure as Vice-Chancellor is coming to an end. The appointment was announced on Thursday by the Grace Bent, Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the university’s Governing Council during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council. Read also: NDC in turmoil as Abdulsalami resigns, SDP appoints Tanko Coordinator of 12,000-Member Campaign Council The announcement was contained in a statement issued by Emmanuel Madugu, Deputy Registrar, Information and Public Relations, on behalf of the Registrar and Secretary to Council. Presenting the letter of appointment to the incoming Vice-Chancellor, Bent charged her to remain focused in the discharge of her responsibilities. The statement quoted the Pro-Chancellor as urging Lar to “be focused”. Her appointment marks a historic milestone for the university, as she becomes its first female Vice-Chancellor and the 11th substantive head of the institution. Gbaoron is the Plateau State correspondent for BusinessDay and a seasoned journalist with a decade of experience covering sub-national affairs across Taraba, Adamawa, Nasarawa, Benue, Plateau, and other states. He holds both National Diploma (ND) and Higher National Diploma (HND) in Mass Communication from Fidel Polytechnic, Gboko. Over the years, he has participated in numerous media trainings and workshops spanning various areas of reporting, strengthening his expertise in economic and political reporting, community-level governance, development stories, and conflict-sensitive journalism. He is a member of Correspondent Chapel in Plateau state, a member of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), he is also a Rotarian and a member of Plateau Club 1921.
